classify.fast.description: Low-cost enum classification with a grammar-friendly local first candidate.

candidates.reason: Small local classification role; the enum grammar carries most of the constraint.
Hosted classification fallback when the local resource is unavailable.
Subscription-backed metered fallback when local and operator BYOK routes are unavailable.

extract.structured.description: Schema-constrained extraction with a mid-size local first candidate.

candidates.reason: Mid-size local generation role; the gateway validates every returned value locally.
Hosted structured-output fallback for schemas the local resource cannot reliably produce.
Subscription-backed metered structured-output fallback.

judge.default.description: Deterministic rubric evaluation with a local-first candidate and hosted fallback.

candidates.reason: Local judge keeps rubric decisions available without a network dependency.
Hosted structured-output fallback when the local judge is unavailable.
Subscription-backed metered judge fallback.

locate.visual.description: Visual grounding that returns canonical target bounds and confidence without exposing provider coordinates.

candidates.reason: Local-first grounding keeps captured frames on the device and uses the measured vision model ladder.
Hosted multimodal grounding fallback for hosts without an available local vision rung.
Subscription-backed metered visual grounding fallback.

write.default.description: Natural-prose generation: marketing copy, blog and technical writing, and creative drafts. Local-first, because BYOK local writing is the intended edge; a caller who needs frontier prose quality sets profile REMOTE_ONLY rather than the catalog reordering for everyone.

candidates.reason: Local prose keeps drafts on the host and is the BYOK path a self-hoster gets with no credential.
Hosted fallback where prose quality is the binding constraint; the model stays a resource policy decision.
Subscription-backed metered fallback when local and operator BYOK routes are unavailable.

write.diverse.description: Diversity-controlled prose generation: one request returns k candidate drafts with verbalized hints. Hosted-first, inverting write.default, because diversity gains are emergent with model capability — a small local rung would underperform on the technique this role exists to serve. Candidate count is carried by instruction; the schema subset cannot enforce it.

candidates.reason: A k-candidate response is neither short nor cheap, and diversity gain scales with model capability; this is the rung the technique is designed for.
Subscription-backed metered fallback, ordered ahead of the local rung because capability matters more than locality for this role specifically.
Local last resort so a host with no credential still gets candidates rather than a failure. Expect measurably lower diversity here; the role's own description says so.

author.generator.description: Long-form code authoring: a parameterized generator program returned as source, validated by the caller before it is ever run. Hosted-first, because the local candidate is sized for short answers and a generator is neither short nor schema-constrained.

candidates.reason: A generator is a program: it must stay internally consistent across a few hundred lines. code.default is the provider's exposed code-authoring role, so the concrete model stays a policy decision rather than a slug in a runtime surface.

Local fallback for a host with no hosted credential. Every authored generator is validated before storage — determinism, declared parameters, no active content, composition at two sizes — so a weaker candidate costs a rejection rather than a bad artifact.
